name: Cessna CitationJet / CJ series / M2
summary: Cessna's best-selling light-jet line, from the original CitationJet through the CJ4, flown by owner-pilots, charter firms and corporate flight departments across the US.

wings: Low, essentially straight (unswept) wing on the CJ1-CJ3 and M2
CJ4 has a moderately swept wing
engines: Two small Williams FJ44 turbofans in pods high on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Slim tube-shaped fuselage with small rounded windows
Long tapered nose with a small baggage door ahead of the windscreen
tail: T-tail: horizontal stabilizer mounted on top of the swept fin

tellTales: T-tail on a small twinjet with a straight, unswept wing
Two small engine pods on the rear fuselage, no winglets
Slim fuselage with small rounded windows and a long pointed nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The CJ series has a T-tail; the older Citation II/V/Bravo/Encore has its tailplane low on the tail cone with strong dihedral.
The CJ/M2 has a straight unswept wing and small windows; the Phenom 100 has a slightly swept wing, very large windows and a curvier nose.
The CJ4 has no winglets and a slimmer fuselage; the Phenom 300 has upturned winglets and much larger cabin windows.
The CJ/M2 has a T-tail; the Mustang's tailplane sits low on the tail cone with dihedral.
The Citation I has a low-set tailplane; the CitationJet has a T-tail.
The Premier I has a swept wing and round windows; the CitationJet has a straight wing and squarer windows.
